memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses said, 'This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.'" - Lev 9:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
So that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.

Moses connects obedience and glory in a single sentence. Do what God has commanded, and God will show Himself.

We must read this carefully. This is not a formula for making God appear — as though the right religious performance could summon Him. God is not obligated by our rituals. But there is a genuine connection in Scripture between obedience and knowing God more deeply.

Jesus made it explicit: Whoever has my commands and keeps them is the one who loves me... and I too will love them and show myself to them (Jn 14:21). Show myself to them. The same promise.

Obedience does not earn God's presence. It positions us to receive it. A person who consistently ignores what God says will find their sense of God growing dim — not because God has withdrawn, but because they have stopped facing His direction.

If your experience of God feels distant, it is always worth asking a simple question before looking for complicated answers: is there something He has told me to do that I have not done?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a clear instruction from God that I have been avoiding?
2. Do I expect to know God better while ignoring what He has already said?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I want to see Your glory. Show me anything I have left undone, and give me a willing heart to obey. Amen.
